title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: A third MikroTik router flaw joins CISA’s exploited list as attacks at the OT remote-access edge continue
items.content_text: CISA added a third MikroTik RouterOS flaw, CVE-2026-67279, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 25 September, with a 28 September federal deadline, joining CVE-2026-86060 and CVE-2026-67277 from 10 September. CERT Polska has tracked in-the-wild exploitation since roughly 2 September of a two-flaw SSH chain it calls “MikroTrick,” and its 22 September write-up shows CVE-2026-67279 chained with CVE-2026-86060 handing an unauthenticated attacker full administrative control. Shadowserver separately counted more than 122,500 MikroTik devices with SSH reachable from the internet in early September — an exposure figure, not a confirmed-unpatched count. These routers commonly front remote-access and cellular-telemetry links into field sites and small, unattended facilities that rarely get timely firmware updates.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog (25 Sep release) and CERT Polska; reported by The Hacker News
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Disclosed and patched early Sep 2026 (CERT Polska, 5 Sep); CVE-2026-86060/67277 added to CISA KEV 10 Sep; CVE-2026-67279 added 25 Sep 2026 (due 28 Sep)

items.title: Colorado confirms foreign hackers tampered with two small water systems’ pumps and alarms
items.content_text: Gov. Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned Colorado water systems in late August, changing equipment settings, disabling remote access and alarms, and altering pumping cycles. Officials say the disruption was brief, with no known impact on water treatment, water quality or public safety. The office says it cannot confirm which foreign actors were involved; federal officials are separately tracking an Iranian-backed effort against US water systems, but no link to these intrusions has been confirmed. It remains the only confirmed OT-tampering incident in this edition, with no new development reported as of 27 September.

items.title: Tanker campaign: a third vessel’s cyberattack claim stays unverified as a Texas regulator urges operators to harden
items.content_text: The Coast Guard and FBI boarded two foreign-flagged energy tankers bound for US ports in late August, including the VL Prosperity, bound for Galveston. A third vessel, the LNG carrier Vivit Africa LNG, lost access to some internal control systems in early September while bound for Italy with a Louisiana cargo, and diverted toward Spain; Bloomberg first reported it on 18 September. The crew’s claim that attackers seized pressure and safety-valve systems is unverified, and Italy’s Coast Guard recorded a cargo-monitoring malfunction of undetermined cause. On 24 September Texas Railroad Commissioner Wayne Christian cited the August boardings in a statement urging the state’s oil and gas operators to “invest, test, monitor and strengthen our defenses now.” No official development has been reported since.
tags: Incident — cyber intrusions on two tankers boarded by the Coast Guard and FBI in August confirmed; a third vessel’s cyberattack claim unverified; a Texas commissioner’s statement cites the boardings; no confirmed operational disruption ashore; attribution unresolved

items.title: A cyber incident stopped container handling at Tanjung Pelepas — the restart began with manual gate-ins
items.content_text: A cyber incident detected late on 9 September forced Malaysia’s Port of Tanjung Pelepas to suspend container terminal operations and its terminal operating systems as a precaution. A phased restart from 10 September initially used manual processing for export container gate-ins, and the port says operations have resumed with system recovery advancing. PTP, a joint venture between MMC Group and APM Terminals, is among the largest transhipment hubs anywhere. For OT defenders it is a clean example of the pattern that actually causes industrial downtime: nothing reported suggests crane or equipment controls were touched — losing the system that decides where each container goes was enough to stop the boxes moving.

items.title: Chained flaws in an IO-Link master give an unauthenticated attacker root — and a say over sensor and actuator data
items.content_text: Nozomi Networks Labs published a technical write-up on 24 September of flaws in the Pepperl+Fuchs IO-Link master ICE2-8IOL-K45P-RJ45 (EtherNet/IP firmware 1.7.3), coordinated through CERT@VDE as VDE-2026-014. Nozomi details 19 CVEs, led by CVE-2026-27546, an authentication bypass rated CVSS v3.1 9.8, alongside OS command-injection flaws rated 8.8 and 7.2 and a path traversal rated 7.5. Chained, they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device, with the ability to manipulate the sensor and actuator data passing through it. CERT@VDE’s 16 September advisories list 20 CVEs, two at CVSS v3.1 9.8, across Pepperl+Fuchs, Phoenix Contact and Carlo Gavazzi IO-Link masters. These devices bridge field sensors to the controller, a layer many OT monitoring programs don’t cover.

items.title: Stolen remote-access logins for US water utilities are already circulating, SpyCloud finds
items.content_text: SpyCloud analyzed stolen-identity data linked to 10,000 US water and wastewater utilities and their technology vendors and found active infostealer exposure at 1,787 of them; 258 had exposed credentials for OT or remote-access systems. In one case, a single infected device at a major US advanced-metering technology provider held saved logins for about 167 utility metering portals. Tools named include TeamViewer, LogMeIn, GoToMyPC and SonicWall and Fortinet management portals. SpyCloud stresses that it measures identity exposure, not confirmed intrusion, and does not tie the findings to any actor or campaign; nothing links them to the Colorado intrusions — but stolen remote-access credentials are one of the most direct routes to the pumps and alarms small utilities depend on.

items.title: Honeywell: most OT programs call themselves mature — four in five still can’t say what’s on the network
items.content_text: Honeywell’s 2026 OT Cybersecurity Benchmark report, published 22 September, found 88% of surveyed organizations describe their OT security program as mature, while only 21% have a complete asset inventory and just 20% continuously monitor connected IoT devices. Significant incidents cost an average 16.2 hours of downtime, at up to $500,000 per hour by Honeywell’s estimate. Energy and utilities respondents reported the highest incident rate at 91%, followed by maritime at 87%. Honeywell frames visibility as the differentiator: organizations with stronger asset and network visibility say they are about four times better positioned to detect, respond to and recover from incidents — a gap worth weighing against any maturity self-assessment.

items.title: Check Point’s federal KEV deadline has passed for two exploited flaws — the VPN gateway that fronts the plant and the server that writes its rules
items.content_text: Check Point has confirmed exploitation of two flaws. CVE-2026-85102, improper certificate validation on Security Gateways and Spark firewalls using site-to-site or remote-access VPN, enables unauthenticated remote code execution; patches shipped 9 September and an exploitation wave from VPN and proxy anonymization infrastructure began on 12 September. CVE-2026-93616, a pre-authentication path traversal in Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management, Log Servers and SmartEvent, lets an unauthenticated attacker upload and execute scripts and was exploited as a zero-day in a handful of pinpointed attacks on 23 July. CISA added both to KEV on 22 September with a 25 September deadline, which has now passed. Check Point gateways commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary and at small unmanned sites.
tags: Advisory — CVE-2026-85102 (Security Gateway and Spark with VPN, certificate validation) and CVE-2026-93616 (management servers and SmartEvent, path traversal), Check Point; both exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 22 Sep 2026, federal deadline 25 Sep 2026, now passed

items.title: Two unpatched NetScaler zero-days are reportedly under attack — and Citrix has not yet published a fix, a CVE or a build list
items.content_text: Research firm watchTowr said on 26 September that two distinct remote-code-execution flaws in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway are being exploited in the wild, discovered during forensic investigations. As of the morning of 27 September, Citrix had published no advisory, CVE, affected-build list, indicators of compromise or fix; fixes are reported to be expected early in the week of 28 September. watchTowr says these are not CVE-2026-19490, the August Gateway/AAA authentication bypass, and it is not known whether builds that fixed that flaw offer any protection. NetScaler 13.1 reached End of Maintenance on 15 September. In our editorial assessment the OT relevance is direct: NetScaler Gateway is a common remote-access front door into OT DMZs and vendor-support paths.
tags: Advisory — two unpatched remote-code-execution zero-days in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway, reported exploited in the wild by watchTowr; no Citrix advisory, CVE, affected-build list or fix as of 27 Sep; not CVE-2026-19490

items.title: About a thousand small Zyxel switches were compromised through a flaw patched in June
items.content_text: GreyNoise reported on 21 September that 996 Zyxel GS1900 managed switches in 48 countries had been compromised through CVE-2026-7273 since about mid-August. The flaw is a stack-based buffer overflow in the switches’ CGI web interface that lets an unauthenticated attacker on the local network potentially execute operating-system commands; firmware 2.90(XXXX.1)C0 and earlier is affected, and Zyxel released a fix in June. CISA added it to KEV on 21 September with a 24 September deadline, now passed. GreyNoise describes the actor as Chinese-speaking and links it to the one behind earlier WordPress and Gitea exploitation. Small managed switches like the GS1900 are common in plant and utility networks, where firmware updates often lag.

items.title: A broken authentication check in the Modicon M580 leaves safety controllers exposed for as long as change control takes
items.content_text: Schneider Electric’s notice SEVD-2026-251-04, published 8 September, discloses CVE-2026-3869: an incorrect implementation of an authentication algorithm (CWE-303) in Modicon M580 and M580 Safety programmable controllers that lets an attacker bypass an authentication check. It scores CVSS v4.0 9.2 and v3.1 9.8. Affected are M580 below application level 4.00 and M580 Safety below application level 4.20. No public exploitation has been reported, but the M580 is a widely deployed controller family, and validation and change-control requirements routinely keep plants on older firmware for weeks or quarters after a fix ships — a gap defenders need to cover with compensating controls.
tags: Advisory — CVE-2026-3869 (CVSS v4.0 9.2; v3.1 9.8), Schneider Electric Modicon M580 and M580 Safety controllers; incorrect authentication-algorithm implementation; fixed firmware available, no known exploitation

items.title: FBI and CISA: your ICS integrator’s access to your plant is your risk too, not just theirs
items.content_text: The FBI and CISA published a joint fact sheet, “Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators,” prompted by a 2025 compromise of a US industrial automation solutions company that provided system integration, engineering consulting and SCADA programming. Between March and April 2025, the agencies say, foreign intruders searched the company’s systems for terms including “customers” and “SCADA” and staged nine archives of roughly 800 files of customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics for exfiltration; the downstream customers named are power utilities and transportation entities. The fact sheet recommends least-privilege access for integrators, on-demand and auditable remote access, a full inventory of supplied hardware and software, security requirements in contracts, and the ability to operate manually if the integrator is compromised.
tags: Guidance — FBI and CISA fact sheet “Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators,” motivated by a 2025 compromise of a US industrial automation/SCADA integrator; no CVE, no new confirmed operator intrusion

items.title: NIST’s core OT security guide gets a major rewrite — and the comment window is open until 30 November
items.content_text: NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security,” on 21 September. The draft expands coverage beyond classic ICS to include building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail, maritime vessels and industrial IoT and cloud convergence; restructures the document around NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with the risk section refocused on the Govern function; and expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and zero-trust architecture for OT. Public comments are open through 30 November 2026. It landed the same week as the FBI and CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk (above).
